title: Data from: The effect of a sports-based cognitive game development program on attention level and prefrontal eeg theta/beta ratio
abstract: This study aims to examine the effects of a 12-week sports-based cognitive game development program on selective attention performance and prefrontal EEG theta/beta ratio in active athletes. The research was conducted using a pre-test–post-test control group randomized experimental design; 100 active athletes from Düzce University were randomly assigned to experimental (n = 50) and control (n = 50) groups; five participants in the experimental group were excluded for non-adherence (absence from more than two sessions), and 95 participants (45 experimental, 50 control) were included in the analysis. The experimental group participated in a sports-based cognitive game development program for 12 weeks, two days a week, totaling 24 sessions, with each session lasting 45 minutes. The program was designed based on a five-stage and gradual cognitive load principle, including adaptation and basic cognitive infrastructure, attention and reaction development, decision-making and strategy, concentration and multitasking performance, and reinforcement and transfer to sports. The control group received no intervention and continued their daily lives. As measurement tools, the d2 Attention Test (TN-E score) and the EEG theta/beta ratio obtained from the Fz electrode using the NeXus-10 Mk II device were used; the data were analyzed using a 2×2 mixed-design ANOVA and Bonferroni-corrected post hoc comparisons.

Human Subjects De-identification Statement:
We confirm that explicit informed consent was obtained from all research participants for the collection and subsequent public deposition of their data under the CC0 1.0 Universal waiver (public domain). To protect participant privacy and comply with ethical standards, all personally identifiable information (PII) and direct identifiers (such as names, contact information, and specific institutional markers) have been completely removed from the dataset. Participants have been assigned randomized numerical identifiers (e.g., P01, P02), and any potentially re-identifiable quasi-identifiers or variables have been appropriately generalized or aggregated prior to publication.
